params.let: 'Check: $a$ is negative, so the graph is reflected and its lowest point is at 90 degrees, which is why this value equals the given minimum.' if a < 0 else 'Check: $a$ is positive, so the graph is not reflected and its highest point is at 90 degrees, which is why this value is above the given minimum.'

stem: For $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$, the graph of $y = {=a}\sin\theta + q$ has a minimum value of ${=m}$. Determine the value of $y$ when $\theta = 90^\circ$.
solution: Without the shift, $y = {=a}\sin\theta$ is the basic sine graph stretched by a factor of ${=b}$ (its amplitude is ${=b}$ whether $a$ is positive or negative), so it runs from ${=-b}$ to ${=b}$.
The shift $q$ moves the lowest value to $-{=b} + q$. This is the given minimum, so $-{=b} + q = {=m}$ and $q = {=m} + {=b} = {=q}$.
notes: Advanced: the twist is the reflection. The minimum of y = a sin θ + q is q - |a| whether a is positive or negative, so q = m + |a|. Then y(90°) = a + q: for a < 0 this equals m (the lowest point moves to 90°), for a > 0 it is m + 2a. One skeleton covers both signs. q = 0 is excluded so every instance has a real shift. Verified numerically over a full period for every parameter pair. Let-strings contain no backslashes; the final step is a plain-words check.
